title: Digital Tribulations 25: Building Technological Sovereignty from Below, The Experience of Argentine Cooperativism – Interview with Cecilia Muñoz from Código Libre
content:
The introduction of Digital Tribulations, a series of intellectual interviews on the developments of digital sovereignty in Latin America, can be read here and the entire series can be found here.

During the month I spent in Buenos Aires, the last city I visited before finally flying back to Europe, I managed to get a firsthand look at its famous cooperativist scene, which extends to platforms. By “famous” I of course mean a niche that has accompanied platform studies since the sharing economy: platform cooperativism. I first came across it through the pioneering work of Trebor Scholz, and I became more familiar with it thanks to the prolific scholarship of my Brazilian friend Rafael Grohmann. He was the one who gave me Cecilia’s contact, along with the phone number of a fellow Italian, Stefano Tortorici, who is writing his PhD on platform cooperativism. As two Italian researchers in our semi-nomadic phase, I bonded with Stefano and ended up hanging out with his numerous artistic housemates, who shared a house not far from the gentrified Palermo neighborhood.
